description: Random seeds used in the paper. Two distinct stages use two distinct seed regimes; conflating them is the most common source of failed reproduction.

evaluation_runs.detail: These are the ten independent runs behind every mean/std reported in the paper's tables and figures. The same ten seeds were used for all methods so that per-log comparisons are paired.
evaluation_runs.verification: Each per-run results file carries a `Seed` column taking exactly these ten values; 1,304 logs x 10 seeds = 13,040 rows per method.
evaluation_runs.how_to_set: main.py --seed <n>, or the DUPLIMEND_SEED environment variable. The seed is applied to python `random`, numpy, torch (CPU and CUDA) and PYTHONHASHSEED via set_all_seeds().

bayesian_optimization.detail: Seed 42 was used ONLY for the 400-trial hyperparameter search that produced duplimend_global.json. It is not one of the ten evaluation runs. main.py still defaults to --seed 42 for backwards compatibility, which is why a default invocation reproduces neither an individual evaluation run nor the reported averages.

note_on_partial_files: Some intermediate result files in the authors' working directory are named '*_5seeds*' and contain only seeds 1-5. Those are superseded snapshots from an earlier stage of the study and were not used for the published numbers. The published numbers come from the full ten-seed files.
